title: Reduce builtin cycle-detector noise (idiomatic mod.rs re-export cycles)
description:
The builtin `no_cycles` constraint (constraint_id `builtin:cycles`, always-on, blocking) consistently fires on idiomatic Rust module re-export cycles: a `mod.rs` doing `pub use child::X` while the children do `use super::Y` forms an import SCC that is NOT architectural debt. We hit this on essentially every manas adoption.

Concrete example from chitta adoption: `builtin:cycles` reported two SCCs — a genuine one (`consolidated → db → facets → tools/search`, real debt, tracked in chitta/50) AND a harmless one (the entire `src/synthesis/` module, purely `mod.rs` re-export wiring). Because the detector is builtin and blocking, the harmless SCC can't be suppressed from `.sutra/rules.toml` and becomes standing noise that dilutes the real finding. The vidhi-sutra-adopt skill already tells authors NOT to add `no_cycles` for this exact reason — but the builtin fires anyway.

Examine options:
- (a) Classify and exclude pure re-export cycles — SCCs whose edges are only `pub use`/re-export edges (no call/type edges) are not real coupling. Requires distinguishing re-export edges from substantive import edges in the graph.
- (b) Allow waiving or suppressing `builtin:cycles` per-SCC from rules.toml (today it appears unwaivable since it's not a user constraint).
- (c) Make the builtin's severity/enablement configurable (e.g. downgrade to advisory, or opt-in).

(a) is the highest-value fix because it removes the noise everywhere without per-project config. Recurring cross-project pain; worth a proper look.
execution_record:
Implemented option (a) but the mechanism differed from the task's guess. Verified against live chitta index (~/.sutra/chitta/index.db): the src/synthesis/ SCC is a star — mod.rs -> each child via `mod self::child` (kind='mod'), children -> mod.rs via `use super::X` (kind='import') for items hoisted into mod.rs. Crucially, `pub use` re-exports do NOT resolve to graph edges at all (the Rust parser keeps "pub use foo::Bar" as raw_path, which fails resolution), so the task's "pure pub use / re-export edge" framing wouldn't have matched anything. The real closing edges are the `mod` module-declarations.

Fix: new Db::module_declaration_edges() (SELECT DISTINCT file_id,resolved_file_id WHERE kind='mod'); evaluate_dd subtracts this set before re-running compute_sccs for cycle findings, unifying with the existing test-edge narrowing (both include_tests and production branches now recompute over base_edges - module_edges). Left the DD engine graph whole so blast-radius/fan-in are unaffected. Two tests added: module_declaration_cycle_not_reported (suppression) and genuine_use_cycle_survives_module_edge_filtering (a real a<->b use-cycle still fires alongside module wiring). Full constraints suite 60 pass, clippy clean on touched files.

Note: verified behavior via unit tests reproducing the exact topology; did not reparse chitta with the new binary to observe the review output there.

context_refs.label: the genuine cycle found alongside the noise

messages.author: agent
messages.text: Review (vidhi-review, claude): approve with notes. Core fix is correct — subtracting kind='mod' edges before SCC re-run removes idiomatic mod.rs re-export noise without per-project config (task option a), verified against parser (rust.rs:1301 emits kind='mod' for bodyless mod decls) and 19 cycle tests pass. One medium finding: the subtraction is PAIR-granular, not edge-kind-granular — module_declaration_edges() returns DISTINCT (file_id,resolved_file_id) where kind='mod', so a parent that both `mod child;` AND `use child::Foo;` collapses to one pair that gets dropped, suppressing a genuine parent<->child mutual-use 2-cycle even though a real use edge exists. Contract mismatch with docstring ("exists *only* because of the mod edge"). Larger SCCs are protected by the re-run; window is parent-child 2-cycles. Tests only cover disjoint pairs. Fix: narrow query to pure-mod pairs (NOT EXISTS non-mod row for same pair) OR document the broader intent + add overlapping-pair test. Low finding: module_declaration_edges() queried one line before the edges.is_empty() early return.
